text:
# Selective and Budgeted Rendering

Also called: Compositing Tree Rendering, Octree-based Entropy Rendering

## Overview
Selective and Budgeted Rendering accelerates volume rendering by leveraging hierarchical data structures to avoid redundant computation, either by reusing unchanged partial images over time or by skipping low-complexity regions based on error metrics. It differs from standard [hierarchical traversal](#896-hierarchical-traversal.md) by introducing temporal persistence ([compositing](#2436-compositing.md) trees) or statistical bounds (entropy) to control rendering budget, whereas siblings like [DDA Tree Traversal with Mini-Stack](5244-dda-tree-traversal-with-mini-stack.md) focus on spatial traversal efficiency without temporal or statistical pruning.

## Shared principles
This family shares the parent's core mechanism of hierarchical descent and ascent [G]. All methods utilize an [octree structure](#2792-octree-based-structures.md) where nodes represent spatial subdivisions. The traversal logic relies on the parent's child selection, empty space skipping, leaf handling, and backtracking mechanisms [G]. Specific to this family, nodes may store auxiliary data (partial images or entropy metrics) that influence the traversal path or the final pixel value computation.

## Subtopics

### [Compositing Tree Rendering](5860-compositing-tree-rendering.md)
A time-varying volume rendering strategy that avoids re-rendering unmodified data by retaining partial images of static subtrees and incrementally compositing them with newly rendered partial images from modified regions. It differs from standard incremental rendering by maintaining a persistent pointer-based octree structure (the compositing tree) that mirrors the data [compression](#4-compression.md) structure, allowing for efficient splicing of new branches and recomposition of ancestors, whereas methods like [Octree-based Entropy Rendering](13580-octree-based-entropy-rendering.md) focus on spatial [resolution adaptation](#3063-resolution-adaptation.md) rather than temporal delta-compositing.

### [Octree-based Entropy Rendering](13580-octree-based-entropy-rendering.md)
[Octree-based Entropy Rendering](#13580-octree-based-entropy-rendering.md) accelerates volume rendering by traversing a hierarchical octree [decomposition](#7254-decomposition.md) where non-leaf nodes store entropy metrics or error measures. It solves the problem of redundant computation in low-entropy occupied space by allowing rays to skip or coarsely sample regions based on these metrics. Unlike sibling methods like [Compositing Tree Rendering](5860-compositing-tree-rendering.md) which may focus on specific compositing structures, this method explicitly uses statistical variance or error bounds to control traversal depth.

### Selective Rendering with Tree Representation
#### definition
- [S1, unofficial] A rendering strategy that uses the tree representation to perform selective rendering efficiently, reducing I/O costs and enabling distribution of data and calculations to multiple workstations.
#### step
- [S1, unofficial] Examine the encoded data to identify partial images built from subtrees which have not changed.
- [S1, unofficial] Reuse the identified unchanged partial images in the following time steps.

## Background
Selective and Budgeted Rendering originated in the context of time-varying volume data visualization, where inter-frame delay and storage space were significant bottlenecks. The approach was developed to leverage hierarchical data structures for both compression and rendering [acceleration](#18-acceleration.md). Preliminary tests showed reductions of up to 90% in storage space and inter-frame delay [S1, unofficial]. The method is particularly relevant for scientific visualization of dynamic datasets where significant portions of the volume remain constant between time steps.
